# New: Match event releases to episodes by title

Part of the [custom Sonarr image](https://github.com/chodeus/Sonarr/tree/custom) (`ghcr.io/chodeus/sonarr:custom`), which merges this branch into `develop`. Reviewed in [#1](https://github.com/chodeus/Sonarr/pull/1).

Series tagged `title-match` can map releases named by event instead of by episode number. `Formula1.2026.Singapore.Grand.Prix`, `Formula1.2026.Round17.Singapore.Race` and `Formula.1.2026x17.Singapore.Qualifying` map to the episode whose TheTVDB title names the same place and session. Without the tag, every series parses exactly as before.

Stock Sonarr reads the year in these names as a season and episode (`2026` becomes S20E26), so every one is rejected as "Unable to identify correct episode(s)".

## How a release is matched

- The 4-digit year picks the season. `Round17`, `R17` or `2026x17` confirms the 17th event weekend: it must agree with the place, and a round with no place matches nothing, because TheTVDB's weekends can drift from the real rounds. A place that is also a language word (Japan, Azerbaijan, Italian) names the event, and isn't taken as the audio language, when "Grand Prix" or "GP" follows it or when the round agrees.
- Weekends group by the venue's known names, so a venue TheTVDB titles two ways (Mexico, Mexico City) stays one round. A session repeating under another of the venue's TheTVDB names starts a second event there, so Bahrain and Sakhir in 2020 are two rounds, and a release with no round is told apart by the place TheTVDB uses. TheTVDB's "Quallifying" reads as qualifying.
- Places match TheTVDB's name or the names releases use, such as Italian/Monza for Italy, Dutch/Zandvoort for Netherlands and Barcelona/Catalunya for Barcelona-Catalunya. A place name that is also a language (Italian, Dutch, Spanish, German…) names the event only right before "Grand Prix" or "GP". Anywhere else it is the audio language, so `Singapore.Race…German` stays German and `Gran.Premio.del.Belgio…ITALIAN` is not Monza.
- Sessions are read most specific first: Sprint Qualifying/Shootout, Sprint, Qualifying/Qualification, Practice 1-3/FP1-3, Warm Up and Race. A name with no session word is the race only if it says "Grand Prix" (or "GrandPrix") or "GP"; otherwise it's a programme TheTVDB doesn't list, such as Tech Talk or Grid Walk. On a sprint weekend, Practice 1 or a bare Practice maps to TheTVDB's single unnumbered Practice.
- A release that matches no event maps to no episode. Sonarr doesn't fall back to the parser's numbers, which read `2026x17` as S2026E17 (China Sprint) whatever the event. The exceptions are explicit numbering such as `S2026E94`; a name that also carries the parsed episode's own TheTVDB title and names no other programme, as Sonarr's `2026x94 - Singapore (Race)` file names do; and a special Sonarr found by its TheTVDB title. The parse keeps its other flags, so a season pack's folder still yields to a file named for its event, and a special the release found by title is looked up again on import. A season pack itself doesn't map.
- A release is never matched if:
  - it is a show, press conference, notebook, grid walk, tech talk, weekend pack, testing, or a sibling series (Academy, F2, F3, Moto2…);
  - it is ambiguous: two places, two sessions, two different years, or a round that disagrees with the place, two different rounds, or a round with no place;
  - it names a session number outside 1-3, such as Practice 4;
  - its event hasn't aired. The check allows a day, because TheTVDB times every session at the series' air time, hours after an Asia-Pacific session has run. TheTVDB episodes without an air date are left out, so one can't split its weekend in two.

## Where it hooks in

- `ParsingService.Map` adopts the corrected `ParsedEpisodeInfo` as soon as the series is known, so the single-episode and season search specifications compare the right numbers. `GetEpisodes` does the same for its other callers.
- Imports replace the file, folder and download-client parses once, in `AggregationService.Augment`, after the scene name is set (it reads `FullSeason`). Every aggregator and import check then sees the same episode and language as the release did, including a daily-dated name such as `Formula1.2026.10.11.Singapore.Grand.Prix`, which the series type check used to reject. If the lookup fails, for example on a locked database, it is logged and the parsed infos are kept, as the aggregators already do.
- The corrected info drops a language that only names the event, so "Italian Grand Prix" no longer marks the release, or its imported file, as Italian audio. A release that names the language again keeps it. Release and import scores therefore agree.
- Subtitles and other extras that don't share the video's name pair with it by episode; their names are read the same way, so `2026x17…Qualifying.English.srt` pairs with the qualifying file and not the race.
- The tag is read through `ITagRepository`, not `ITagService`, because `TagService` depends on the indexer factory and every indexer depends on `ParsingService`. The cached tag is cleared on `TagsUpdatedEvent`, and a lookup that raced the change isn't kept, so creating or renaming `title-match` takes effect at once.

## Tests

- `EpisodeTitleMatcherFixture` runs against TheTVDB's full 2026 season, through the real parser (a title the parser rejects fails the test). It covers 22 release names that must match, 25 that must map to no episode, explicit numbering, a special found by its title, the language cases, the tag gate and the not-aired guard.
- `EventTitleMappingFixture` runs the real parser, `ParsingService`, matcher, import aggregation and extras services, with only the database mocked. Every must-match name goes through both the release path and the import path. It also covers a daily-dated file, files Sonarr named (`S2026E14` and `2026x94` styles, and a name that carries an episode's title but is another programme), a lone file in a season pack's folder, the special a release found by title, a sibling session without an air date, the quality revision, a failed episode lookup during an extras scan, a tag created during a lookup, audio languages that aren't the event's, a language word alone, names with no session word, no fallback to parsed numbers, the release and import languages of an "Italian Grand Prix" download, a special found by its title, extras named unlike their video, and creating the tag.
- `GetEpisodesFixture` covers the mapping, the single-episode search specification on a matched release, the file path, and the fallback to parsed numbers for a series without the tag.
- The parser, decision engine, download, extras, media file, indexer search and messaging suites pass (3,610 tests), and so does `ContainerFixture`. The 10 that fail (9 `CompletedDownloadServiceTests` and Deluge reconnect) also fail on unmodified develop: upstream code there logs warnings those tests don't expect. Each new rule was broken on purpose (35 mutations), and its tests failed every time.
